correctness.rationale: On the choice set expressly stipulated in the frozen assumptions, the all-goods ray t1 is feasible for all t≥0. The price-adjusted utility along it is t times the sum of α_i−p_i minus (n/2)(1+(n−1)γ)t². On 2+(n−1)γ<0 the quadratic coefficient is strictly positive for every finite price vector, proving unboundedness and therefore no global optimum. The branch is nonempty under |γ|<1 precisely for some γ when n≥4. The other n−1 eigenvalues are 1−γ>0, so strict concavity holds exactly when 1+(n−1)γ>0. The proof invalidates this unconstrained optimization interpretation, not an algebraic model with inverse demand taken as primitive. The source package identifies §2 for the first-order conditions and §3.1 for the branch; these reported locations were not independently recovered, and the verdict does not certify that the actual article rules out budget constraints.
residual_risks: The literal article specification and inequality passage were not independently read. The verified result assumes the unbounded nonnegative choice set; it does not show that a different finite-budget or constrained consumer program has no maximizer.

value.rationale: This distinguishes a formally analyzable firm's best-response branch from a branch implementable by the specified representative consumer. It rules out an open parameter region, not a degenerate test point. The result helps prevent interpreting a dynamical stability calculation as a consumer-founded equilibrium without checking demand's admissible domain.
residual_risks: It does not determine the formal map's stability or the outcome of any constrained demand system.
